description: Morals Pointed and Tales Adorned. The Būstān of Sa'dī, translated from Persian by G. M. Wickens (Toronto, 1974; reprinted 1978), in 344 bookmarked and searchable pdf pages. This is volume 17 in Columbia University's Persian Heritage Series, Ehsan Yarshater, editor. Scanned by Robert Bedrosian. Wikipedia has a main entry on the renowned Iranian poet Saadi of Shiraz (1210-1291/92), and a group of related entries. Encyclopaedia Iranica has an article on Sa'di by Paul Losensky, and on his main works, Būstān (by G.M. Wickens), and Golestān (by Franklin Lewis). On the poet and his themes, see also Minoo Southgate's article, Men, Women, and Boys: Love and Sex in the Works of Sa'di.

description: The present study aimed to investigate the frequency of the use of two semantic adjustment strategies; namely, expansion and reduction, in the two English translations of book one of "Masnavi." For this purpose, 300 lines of "Masnavi" by Rumi (2014) along its two corresponding English translations by Nicholson (2004) and Whinfield (2001) were critically analyzed based on Nida and Taber's (2003) theoretical framework. Based on the outcomes of the present study, both translators applied the expansion strategy more than the reduction because poems in "Masnavi" were so condensed and the writer of "Masnavi" applied classic words which were not understandable to the target language readers.
